page: Vultr vcg-a40-4c-20g-8vram is a fractional GPU instance featuring 4 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs (2 physical cores, 2 threads per core) running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 20.0 GB of system memory, 360 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. This setup offers a balanced resource profile for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the overhead of a full physical GPU.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific workloads, particularly LLM inference. The instance achieves top-tier results for small (135M) and medium (7B) model prompt processing and text generation, reaching 3161.22 tokens per second for 7B prompt processing and 107.91 tokens per second for 7B text generation. General compute and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores, fall into the average tier. However, database operations and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is poor.

By utilizing a fractional GPU (0.1667 of an NVIDIA A40), this instance provides a cost-effective entry point for developers and engineers needing GPU-accelerated compute without the expense of dedicated hardware. It is highly suited for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning prototyping, and lightweight CUDA-based data processing. It is less optimal for high-throughput web serving or heavy database workloads due to its weaker performance in those specific areas.
